rules.name: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (Nutritional Support to TB Patients)

rules.message: Person with TB (all notified TB patients are beneficiaries)
Must be notified / registered on the NIKSHAY portal (public or private sector)
Support is paid only while the person is on anti-TB treatment

benefits.text: Rs 1,000 per month for every TB patient, paid by direct benefit transfer (DBT), for the duration of anti-TB treatment.
For children with TB who have no bank account, the money is paid into a parent's or guardian's account.

historical_benefits.text: Rs 500 per month for each notified TB patient for the duration of anti-TB treatment (original amount from 1 April 2018).

required_documents.name: Bank account details (preferably an Aadhaar-linked bank account)
For children without a bank account: parent's or guardian's bank account details

how_to_apply.text: The TB patient (public or private sector) must be notified on the NIKSHAY platform; bank account and Aadhaar details are entered in NIKSHAY by health staff.
If the patient has no bank account or Aadhaar number, health staff help open a bank account (preferably under Jan Dhan Yojana) and help with Aadhaar enrolment.

evidence.quote: All notified TB patients are beneficiaries of the scheme.

All TB patients notified on or after 1st April 2018 including all existing TB patients under treatment are eligible to receive incentives. The patient must be registered\notified on the NIKSHAY portal.

evidence.claim: Paid during treatment; DBT; Aadhaar-enabled bank account preferred; original Rs 500 amount
evidence.quote: Financial incentive of Rs.500/- per month for each notified TB patient for duration for which the patient is on anti-TB treatment. ... The incentives can be distributed in Cash (only via DBT preferably through Aadhaar enabled bank accounts) or in-kind.
The NPY benefits have doubled, now every TB patient is supported at the rate of Rs. 1000 per month, which is paid through direct benefit transfer.
The Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) provides a monthly incentive of Rs 1,000 to support dietary needs during TB treatment

evidence.claim: Public or private sector; notified on NIKSHAY
evidence.quote: Each TB patient whether public or private sector notified must be notified on the Nikshay, platform.
This scheme is implemented across all States and UTs in India.

For paediatric TB patients where Bank accounts are not available, the money shall be deposited in parents / guardians accounts whose details are to be sought and entered in Nikshay against the patient’s records.

For patients not having Bank account or Aadhaar number, health staff will facilitate opening of Bank a/c for the patient preferably under Jan Dhan Yojna and will also facilitate his/her Aadhaar enrolment.

flags.detail: Rs 500 (2018 guidelines) vs Rs 1,000 (PIB 7 October 2024; TB Mukt Bharat strategy June 2025). Reviewer decision: Rs 1,000 per month is the current benefit; Rs 500 is kept as historical information.

flags.public_note: The date from which the Rs 1,000 monthly amount applies is not yet confirmed from an official source. The increase was announced on 7 October 2024.
flags.detail: Effective date of the Rs 1,000 rate. 7 October 2024 is the announcement date. A later release reportedly gives 1 November 2024, but this was not retrieved or confirmed, so effective_from is left empty.
The payment instalment schedule and the in-kind minimum food-basket value (Rs 500) in src-npy-scheme-details pages 1-2 are based on the old Rs 500 rate and were not included.

notes: No age, income, category, gender or state restriction was found in the sources; the scheme applies across all States and UTs.
The 'notified on or after 1 April 2018' condition is historical (all current patients meet it) and is not modelled as a rule.
Treatment status and NIKSHAY registration cannot be answered by the questionnaire, so they are manual checks; the best possible automatic result is need_more_info, never eligible.
